items.note: The page follows the paper's route: normalized cost table, margin list, justification of each row from the lemmas, setup and exceptional repair shown to be o(V), then the total O(Tp p^{1-kappa}) with a schoolbook cutoff. The closing paragraph explains that g_2 is the product of three small numbers epsilon, c, 1-tau, which is why the exponent is so close to one.

dropped: the two absorbed rows of the paper's table (final scaling and rounding, normalized p^delta; input, padding, carries and output, normalized 1)
that a fixed number of repeated transforms and convolutions is included in the constants
that d^2 is absorbed by d^2 ell^tau (only implicit in 'Here d^2 ell^tau = p^{2 epsilon} p^{(1-epsilon) tau}')
items.note: The page gives the sizes d, K, ell, alpha as powers of p and tabulates the seven normalized costs, their powers and margin expressions exactly as in the paper's Table; it works out the exponent for the axis row and log(rp)=O(p^{1-epsilon}) 'since r <= 2^{O(p/d)}'. The other powers are left to direct substitution, which is enough here.

Shows the products 'g_2=2^{-75}2^{-56}2^{-50}=2^{-181}' and 'g_3=2^{-75}2^{-54}=2^{-129}' from the stated parameters. It asserts g_1>1/2, g_4>2^{-51}, g_5>1/8, g_6>1/2 by substitution, as the paper does, and concludes min g_i = 2^{-181} = 2 kappa.

dropped: generation of the chirp exponentials (also O(p^{1+delta}) per entry), which is part of the paper's per-entry chirp cost
that twists and scalar pointwise products fit the chirp row (the page's row is just 'Chirps')
the condition that a single excess bit is peeled only when the two axis widths differ by one
the d CRT rotations at O(dV)
items.note: Each row is justified as in the paper: O(p/K) exchanges at O(VK^tau) give O(pK^{tau-1}); O(d^2) axis moves at O(V(1+ell^tau)); sum over axes of T/t_i lines at O(t_i p^{3/2+delta} alpha); d squares and products on O(p) bits with the established multiplier; and T/r records with four O(rp)-bit products using the established multiplier at length o(n), giving O(Tp log(rp)).

dropped: that there is only a fixed number of tensor maps (needed to turn 2dT/r lines per map into O(dTp^C/r) in total)
that extraction and reinsertion scans of the full volume are already charged to node overhead
that the internal recursion of the established multiplier and the Gaussian iterations are charged in their own running times
items.note: Reproduces the paper's split: at most p^A visits at p^C each give p^{A+C}=o(Tp); per-record and per-line work is O(Tp^{A+C}/r) and O(dTp^C/r), both o(Tp) since r exceeds every power of p; the exceptional stream has length O(V_call d 2^{-K}), O(p) sorting scans, summed to O(V p^{O(1)} 2^{-K})=o(V). Global setup and prime search are stated as o(V), as the paper does ('as proved earlier').

dropped: p = Theta(log n), which is needed to turn O(Tp p^{1-kappa}) into O(n (log n)^{1-kappa}) (the page gives only Tp = Theta(n))
that the cutoff is fixed beyond all the size, precision, margin and layout conditions
the definition lg n = max{ceil(log_2 n), 1}, needed for the bound to cover every n >= 1
items.note: Combines the powers bounded by 1-2 kappa with 'any fixed power of log p is at most p^kappa eventually, which the margin 2 kappa leaves room for' to get O(Tp p^{1-kappa}). Small lengths are handled by schoolbook multiplication below a fixed cutoff, absorbed into the constant, as in the paper.

errors.quote: the repair costs $O(Vp^{O(1)}2^{-K})=o(V)$, because $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ beats every power of $p$
errors.problem: K = Theta(p^{epsilon c}) is far smaller than p, so K does not beat every power of p. What beats every power of p is 2^K, because K grows faster than log p. The paper says only 'Here d=O(p^epsilon) and K=Theta(p^{epsilon c}) with epsilon c>0', which is what makes p^{A'} 2^{-K} -> 0.

errors.quote: Each move peels one excess bit, exchanges the equal-width parts and restores it
errors.problem: In the paper the excess bit is peeled only 'when widths differ by one'; equal-width axes are exchanged directly. The page makes the peeling unconditional.

errors.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ be the volume, the number of stored bits of $T$ coefficients of $p$ bits
errors.problem: The paper's coefficient formats use Theta(p) bits per coefficient, not exactly p, so the padded array has Theta(V) stored bits. V = Tp is the normaliser and equals the stored bit count only up to a constant.
